# Independent audit: optimized parameters under actual body variation

Audited source:
`candidate b2439018eaa1681d`.
Full independent mathematical read, with priority to Sections5–8:
**PASS. No correction identified.** This is a conditional continuity theorem,
not an optimized-value derivative or a new OC payment theorem.

1. The fixed-body size-bias identity is correct. With R=U/L, the old
   certificate yields E R<=sum sigma_i R(Y_i). Log normalization supplies
   E log R=0. The stated reverse KL is log E R, and the Pinsker constants
   use L1 distance rather than half the L1 distance. The interior modulus
   follows from bounded concave-function slopes on smaller balls. Boundary
   uniform convergence is properly excluded by the exact interval example.

2. The ambient homothety used for the reference parameter is legal even
   though it changes base coordinates: it is ONLY composition of a concave
   function, not a transformation of the measured mixed family. The support
   inequality lambda e<=(1-lambda)r maps the new canonical hull into the
   old one. Positivity, continuity and mixed logarithmic normalization are
   retained. Fixed-base symmetric-difference convergence and the uniform
   continuous slab bound control all integer tilts without bounding their
   coefficients. Pure-base cuts retain their actual closed boundary mass.

3. The common fiber contraction pushes every old row to the actual new
   family. Its base barycenter remains the original integer p_i. Its
   continuous barycenter is (1-t)y_i+t E_rho g_Z, which belongs to the new
   fiber by actual convexity. No affine centroid graph is claimed. The
   proper-depth gap at the limiting mark and strict increase with scalar
   buffer give the pointwise upper bound on U_m at these perturbed marks.
   This can use the uniform strictness argument in
   `historical context (not an accepted premise)`;
   it does not require a common new globally deepest source.

4. Jensen is applied to U_m on its actual new convex hull and each pushed
   probability row. It is not applied to the generally nonconcave full
   composition U_m o T_m across different bases. This gives (17), before
   any compactness assumption on U_m. The inner/outer homothetic sandwich
   then gives (18): the Jacobian factor in the integral and the inner
   volume cancels, leaving the printed V_z denominator.

5. Log normalization and the upper sampled bound give a positive lower
   bound for each fiber maximum. The homothetic superlevel estimate gives
   sublevel measure O(r), uniformly, hence log uniform integrability with
   the stated O(r(1+|log r|)) tail. In particular a small-volume collar
   cannot hide unbounded negative logarithmic mass.

6. The same contraction factor on every fiber is essential and correctly
   used. Writing j_m=(1-t_m)^d, change of variables and current normalization
   give exactly

       E_(dm/M) log[U_m(T_m w)/L(w)]
         =-(M j_m)^(-1) int_(S_m outside T_m S) log U_m.

   There is no missing current-mass multiplier, because the current
   logarithmic integral itself is zero. Thus the pulled-back entropy
   tends to zero. Combining it with (17) yields the stated KL and L1
   bounds. On each OLD fiber the composition is concave, so the interior
   estimate applies there. The common interior Lipschitz bounds pass from
   the contracted coordinate to the same original coordinate.

7. Zero-extended L1 and logarithmic L1 convergence follow from the small
   inner/outer collars, the uniform bound and log UI. The source explicitly
   means zero extension OF log U, not log of the zero extension. Uniform
   marked-energy vanishing at fiber boundaries converts interior parameter
   convergence to uniform actual-buffer convergence; the all-direction
   slab argument then controls the optimized depth values. This uses the
   separately established joint marked-energy continuity exactly within
   its positive-fiber Hausdorff regime.

The theorem assumes a limiting certificate with proper deepest marks,
fixed finite base, positive full-dimensional limiting fibers, and nearly
optimal normalized positive concave parameters. It does not prove new
minimizer attainment, boundary-uniform parameter convergence, a rate for
body derivatives, or equality of volume and surface transports.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
